units.translation: Apollonius, the poet of the Argonautica, was by birth an Alexandrian of the Ptolemaic tribe, son of Silleus, or as some say, Illeus. He lived in the time of the third Ptolemy, a pupil of Callimachus. At first he was associated with Callimachus, his own teacher, ... but late he turned to composing poems. It is said that while still a youth he presented the Argonautica and was condemned; unable to bear the shame of the citizens and the reproach and slander of the other poets, he left his homeland and went down to Rhodes, and there he polished and corrected them, and thus presented them and won great renown; therefore he calls himself Rhodian in his poems.

5 Suda 3419: Apollonius of Alexandria, epic poet, who spent time in Rhodes, son of Silleus, in the time of Ptolemy called Euergetes (the phrase "in the time of Ptolemy called Euergetes" is read after Timarchus, from where W restored it), pupil of Callimachus, contemporary of Eratosthenes and Euphorion and Timarchus, and successor of Eratosthenes in the directorship of the library in Alexandria. Pap. Oxyrh. 1241, II 1 among the directors of the Alexandrian library: "Apollonius son of Silleus, Alexandrian, called the Rhodian, acquaintance of Callimachus. He also became the teacher of the third (first in the papyrus, corrected by Hunt) king. He was succeeded by Eratosthenes, etc."

He taught brilliantly there and was deemed worthy of Rhodian citizenship and honor. LGP

Apollonius the poet was by birth an Alexandrian, son of Silleus or Illeus, and his mother was Rhode. He studied under Callimachus, who was a grammarian in Alexandria, and after composing these poems he presented them. Having failed utterly and being ashamed, he went to Rhodes and there became a citizen and taught rhetoric, whence they wish to call him Rhodian. Then, while living there and polishing his poems, he presented them and won great renown, so that he was deemed worthy of Rhodian citizenship and honor. But some say that he returned to Alexandria and again presented them there and won the highest renown, so that he was deemed worthy of the libraries and the Museum and was buried with Callimachus himself. LGP.
